acceptanceCriteria: Root cause of the clean=true listings=0 path under load is identified and recorded (which branch of executePool admits the group without a listing when the child start races the 3s timeout).

TestCALV0188_GroupListingOverrun passes 20 consecutive runs under `go test -count=20 -run TestCALV0188_GroupListingOverrun$ ./internal/tasks/store/` while a parallel `go test ./cmd/corvint/` run loads the host, or the test is restructured so the assertion no longer depends on wall-clock ordering.
The package-level run `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/tasks/store/` completes under 600s on an otherwise quiet host or the Makefile timeout note documents the measured duration.
body: Observed 2026-10-12 on branch claude/v1-1265-freeze (b8ef66364, PR beamfall/corvint#828; the change touches no internal/tasks file) during a full `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/tasks/store/` run that took 795s on a loaded host (a parallel cmd/corvint run and a builder lane were active). Failure: pool_process_test.go:308 `surviving member admitted: clean=true listings=0` in 0.01s. The same test passes 3/3 in isolation on the branch and 2/2 on the clean origin/main worktree (5e664ce9c), so it is a load/timing-sensitive flake, not a regression: the survivor `/bin/sh -c "/bin/sleep 60 & echo $! > marker"` with TimeoutSeconds 3 is expected to leave the process group unproved and force a listing, but under load the retired-group path reported clean with no listing. A first run without -timeout also hit the 10m panic (`test timed out after 10m0s`) in the same package. Expected: the test either proves the survivor deterministically (e.g. waits for the marker before the timeout fires, or pins the group-listing hook) or is marked load-sensitive with a bounded retry; actual: intermittent FAIL under load. Logs: scratchpad agent-1265/int/store-retry.log and misc.log (session b89960c8).
title: internal/tasks/store TestCALV0188_GroupListingOverrun fails under host load (surviving member admitted, listings=0)
